9748               cv567
9749               	;
9750               	; 	' THE SIXTEENTH-PIXEL ACCUMULATOR. hx is one unsigned byte per screen
9751               	; 	' (2), so there is nowhere to keep a fraction -- the fraction lives here
9752               	; 	' and is spent as whole pixels. THREE IFs, not a loop and not a divide:
9753               	; 	' `%` and `/` both compile to a real TMS9900 DIV (CLAUDE.md 3A) and this
9754               	; 	' runs every pass.
9755               	; 	'
9756               	; 	' THE NUMBER OF DRAINS IS A CEILING ON THE SPEED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE
9757               	; 	' POINT OF THIS COMMENT. Each IF can spend one whole pixel, so N drains
9758               	; 	' cap hspd at N px per pass NO MATTER WHAT hsp64 SAYS. The invariant is:
9759               	; 	'
9760               	; 	'     hacc is under 16 on entry, and hsp64 is at most 48,
9761               	; 	'     so hacc is under 64 here and three drains always suffice.
9762               	; 	'
9763               	; 	' KEEP hsp64 <= 48. This was quarter-pixels with TWO drains and the same
9764               	; 	' invariant written the same way -- "hsp4 is at most 8, so it can never
9765               	; 	' need a third" -- and it was correct until somebody set hsp4 = 9 without
9766               	; 	' re-reading it. The crook then ran at a flat 2.0 px/pass while every
9767               	; 	' comment, the design table and assets/checkchase.py all said 2.25, and
9768               	; 	' the surplus quarter leaked into hacc and wrapped the byte every 256
9769               	; 	' passes. Nothing failed; he simply arrived two thirds of a screen short
9770               	; 	' of his own escape. checkchase.py now counts these IFs and refuses a
9771               	; 	' speed the drains cannot deliver.
9772               	; 	'
9773               	; 	' 7, NOT 6, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED. Tracked off the reference video
9774               	; 	' (DESIGN.md 4a), the 2600's Kelly covers 0.40 screen widths a second and
9775               	; 	' its Harry 0.193 -- a ratio of 2.07. At hsp4 = 6 ours was 2.67, and the
9776               	; 	' crook visibly strolled. 7 brings it to 2.29. 8 would match the original
9777               	; 	' exactly and cannot be used: Kelly's route here is 1.95x Harry's, so a
9778               	; 	' speed ratio of 2.0 leaves the on-foot chase 0.2 s of slack, which is no
9779               	; 	' chase at all. checkchase.py holds the line.
9780               	; 	' STILL RUNNING FROM THE STAIRS -- and this has to come BEFORE the move,
9781               	; 	' not after it. It sat below the two `IF hmv` blocks, where all it could
9782               	; 	' still reach was the animation counter: he faced the right way, played
9783               	; 	' the run cycle and did not travel a pixel. He stood at the foot of the
9784               	; 	' flight looking busy.
9785               	; 	'
9786               	; 	' TWO THINGS END THE RUN, AND BOTH ARE VISIBLE ON SCREEN.
9787               	; 	'
9788               	; 	' THE KOP ARRIVING ON THIS FLOOR OUTRANKS IT. This used to override the
9789               	; 	' flee as well as the climb, so for the whole of the run he held one
9790               	; 	' heading no matter where Kelly was -- and ran straight into him without
9791               	; 	' appearing to notice he was there. The flee above has already worked out
9792               	; 	' which way is away; clearing the run simply lets it stand.

9880               	;
9881               	; 	' HE WALKS BY REAL TIME, NOT BY LOOP PASS -- one accumulate-and-drain per
9882               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAME rather than per pass. Everything that moves here used to be
9883               	; 	' per pass while the CLOCK is paced by the frame delta, so a busy screen
9884               	; 	' slowed Harry in real seconds and the clock did not slow with him: the
9885               	; 	' same uninterrupted escape finished with nine timer units in hand from a
9886               	; 	' light screen and none at all from the lift screen, decided by where the
9887               	; 	' player happened to be standing. Now he covers the same ground per second
9888               	; 	' wherever anybody is (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
9889               	; 	'
9890               	; 	' A LOOP, NOT A MULTIPLY. `*` compiles to a real TMS9900 MPY, and reading a
9891               	; 	' 16-bit variable straight after one returns the product's HIGH word
9892               	; 	' (CLAUDE.md 3A). fdv is 1..3 here, so this is at most three adds.
9893               	; 	'
9894               	; 	' SIXTY-FOURTHS, AND ONLY TWO DRAINS -- both fall out of accumulating per
9895               	; 	' FRAME instead of per pass. He covers under a pixel a frame, so two drains
9896               	; 	' are ample where the per-pass version needed three; and the finer unit is
9897               	; 	' what makes the speed tunable at all. In sixteenths one step was about six
9898               	; 	' SECONDS of his route, so nothing landed near the buzzer; in sixty-fourths
9899               	; 	' it is about one and a half. Keep hsp64 <= 128: hacc is under 64 on entry,
9900               	; 	' so 64 + 128 stays inside a byte and two drains always suffice.
9901               	; 	'
9902               	; 	' AND THE STEP IS CLAMPED TO THREE FRAMES' WORTH, WHICH IS NOT A DETAIL.
9903               	; 	' Two tests sample his position once a pass and neither interpolates:
9904               	; 	'
9905               	; 	'   ARRIVAL   `hdx < 6` around the escalator or the roof door -- an ELEVEN
9906               	; 	'             pixel window. A step over 10 px can jump clean across it and
9907               	; 	'             he never arrives at all.
9908               	; 	'   THE CATCH `hdd < CATCHR` is 12, a 23-wide band, and Kelly closes 4 of
9909               	; 	'             it himself -- so Harry over ~18 px could pass through the Kop
9910               	; 	'             between two passes without either sample being inside it.
9911               	; 	'
9912               	; 	' The clamp and the drains live in pace_step now, with the reasoning; the
9913               	; 	' numbers above are what sized them. Measured: TIME 02 on the lift screen
9914               	; 	' against TIME 04 on a light one when the clamp was 3, and 00 against 09
9915               	; 	' before any of this.
9916               	; 	'
9917               	; 	' The ESCALATOR RIDE is deliberately untouched: it returns above this,
9918               	; 	' clocked one step per pass to stay locked to the moving staircase. A rider
9919               	; 	' advanced by the frame delta either drifts off the treads or makes the
9920               	; 	' steps run backwards (CLAUDE.md 3A, DESIGN.md 0f). It is about 3% of his
9921               	; 	' journey.
9922               	; 	'
9923               	; 	' `hanim` still advances by hspd and is still an ODOMETER -- pixels
9924               	; 	' travelled, not time -- so the run cycle stays locked to the ground at any
9925               	; 	' rate. A 9 px step moves it exactly one pose of its 8 px beat.

10386               	;
10387               	; 	' ======================================================================
10388               	; 	' COLLISIONS -- pure arithmetic against RAM, no VDP reads
10389               	; 	' ======================================================================
10390               	; 	' Kelly's box is [kfh, kfh + kh) above the slab; an obstacle's is
10391               	; 	' [ohb, oht). The ball's inset hitbox is what makes 8..10 avoidable both
10392               	; 	' ways -- without it there is a height at which the ball can be neither
10393               	; 	' jumped nor ducked, and an unavoidable hazard is not difficulty.
10394               	; 	' ONE HIT PER CONTACT, WITH A REFRACTORY PERIOD.
10395               	; 	'
10396               	; 	' The overlap test is true on every frame the player is touching
10397               	; 	' something, so with no latch at all one clumsy cart charges nine seconds
10398               	; 	' several times over -- and what the player sees is the clock jumping by
10399               	; 	' 27, from which the only available conclusion is that the penalty is
10400               	; 	' broken.
10401               	; 	'
10402               	; 	' A latch that clears on the first non-overlapping frame is still not
10403               	; 	' enough, and the case that breaks it is the BOUNCING BALL: it rises off
10404               	; 	' the player between bounces, which is a genuine loss of contact, so a
10405               	; 	' player standing still under one is taxed on every single bounce while
10406               	; 	' being given no opportunity to do anything about it. Technically two
10407               	; 	' collisions; in play, one situation.
10408               	; 	'
10409               	; 	' So obht() is a countdown, not a flag. A hit sets it to HITREF; it ticks
10410               	; 	' down only while the player is CLEAR, and the same obstacle cannot charge
10411               	; 	' again until it reaches zero. Contact holds the count up, so parking
10412               	; 	' inside something never earns a second penalty either.
10413               	; coll_obst:
10414               cvb_COLL_OBST

10754               	; 	' THE FLOOR CLEARS WHEN YOU ARE HIT, and stays clear until you re-enter
10755               	; 	' the screen. Nine seconds is a heavy penalty on a fifty-unit clock, and
10756               	; 	' taking it while still standing among the things that charged it -- with
10757               	; 	' a second hazard 48 px behind the first -- is how one mistake becomes
10758               	; 	' three. Clearing the row makes the penalty a single event you can walk
10759               	; 	' away from.
10760               	; 	'
10761               	; 	' BOTH SLOTS, WHATEVER IS IN THEM. Radios used to be exempt: they are
10762               	; 	' CHARACTERS stamped into the name table rather than sprites, so zeroing
10763               	; 	' the kind would have stopped them colliding while leaving them plainly
10764               	; 	' visible on the shelf, and a fixture that is still there has to still be
10765               	; 	' there. That was a reason to UNDRAW them, not a reason to keep them --
10766               	; 	' and it left the one hazard that cannot leave on its own as the only one
10767               	; 	' the mercy did not cover. haz_off now takes the characters with it.
10768               	; 	'
10769               	; 	' NOTHING RESTORES IT HERE. load_band repopulates the band from the
10770               	; 	' template, and it runs only on a seam crossing or a round start, so
10771               	; 	' "until the screen is re-entered" costs no state and no timer: leave and
10772               	; 	' come back and the hazards are simply placed again.
10773               	; 	'
10774               	; 	' THE CALL ITSELF IS IN THE MAIN LOOP, at the end of the freeze -- see
10775               	; 	' the hfz block there for why.
10776               	; 	' A HIT DOES NOT END A JUMP. This used to force ST_RUN and zero the arc,
10777               	; 	' which dropped him straight down out of mid-air onto whatever he happened
10778               	; 	' to be over -- and since the arc is ballistic and ignores the stick once
10779               	; 	' he is airborne (0l), that read as the game taking the controls away
10780               	; 	' rather than as a hit landing. The penalty is the nine units and the
10781               	; 	' knock flash; where he comes down is still his own arc.
10782               	; 	'

10943               	; 	' AND THEY HAVE TO BE AT THE SAME HEIGHT, NOT MERELY ON THE SAME FLOOR.
10944               	; 	'
10945               	; 	' `hlv` does not change until a ride ENDS -- a crook stepping onto a
10946               	; 	' flight keeps the floor he left until he arrives at the next one. So
10947               	; 	' while he was most of a storey up or down the stairs he still counted as
10948               	; 	' standing on the floor he started from, and a Kop who ran over the head
10949               	; 	' of the flight arrested him through the floor. Reported from play:
10950               	; 	' "I run over top of him, even though we do not touch".
10951               	; 	'
10952               	; 	' It is the same shape of bug as the catch that fired at MAXIMUM
10953               	; 	' separation: a test that is right about one axis and silent about the
10954               	; 	' other, where the silent one happens to be true nearly all the time.
10955               	; 	'
10956               	; 	' UNSIGNED-SAFE. Riding up is above the shared floor and riding down is
10957               	; 	' below it, which is a signed quantity, and CVBasic's variables are not.
10958               	; 	' So both are collected as POSITIVE heights on opposite sides -- Kelly's
10959               	; 	' climb plus Harry's descent on one side, Harry's climb on the other --
10960               	; 	' and the difference is taken between two numbers that cannot go
10961               	; 	' negative. Two riders passing on the same flight measure the sum of

11071               	; 	' placed him at his old floor and then hid him again. That is not free.
11072               	; 	' CVBasic's SPRITE writes a RAM mirror which the vblank ISR copies to
11073               	; 	' VRAM, so a vblank landing BETWEEN the draw and the hide latches the
11074               	; 	' visible state for a frame -- and draw_actors is long (Kelly, Harry,
11075               	; 	' eight obstacles) while a pass on the lift screen spans two or three
11076               	; 	' frames, so it happened constantly. He flickered at the floor he had
11077               	; 	' just left, which reads as a drawing bug rather than as a journey.
11078               	; 	'

11131               	; 	' KELLY'S HAT DOES NOT FLASH WHEN HE IS HIT. It used to alternate to white
11132               	; 	' on the `fphs AND 2` phase for the twenty frames of `knock`, on the

11135               	; 	' digits still drop by nine, and the hit now has a sound that is allowed to
11136               	; 	' finish. Three signals for one event, and the flash was the least legible
11137               	; 	' of them -- a two-frame colour swap on a 16 px hat, during the one moment
11138               	; 	' the player is looking at where they are being pushed.
11139               	; 	'

11141               	; 	' colour goes straight into the SPRITE calls below and the per-pass
11142               	; 	' variable, its assignment and two nested IFs all go.

11145               	; 	' KELLY IS SPRITES 0, 1 AND 2 and nothing else ever is -- the VDP drops
11146               	; 	' the highest-numbered sprites on an over-full scanline, so the lowest
11147               	; 	' slots are the ones that can never disappear, and the player is the one
11148               	; 	' thing that must never disappear.

11151               	; 	' between them cover rows 0-15; slot 2 sits at ky+16. Boxes 0/1 and box 2
11152               	; 	' never share a scanline, so an actor costs at most TWO boxes on any line

11154               	; 	' cost just as much as a full one. Two actors meeting is four, exactly

11679               	; 	' keep their y, so the planted foot stays on the floor and the figure

11686               	; 	' figure, which is the flapping of DESIGN.md 0j2 in the vertical.

12192               	; 	' is at all -- he can be one pixel off-screen and completely invisible.

12195               	; 	' is at base 4096 and no third-selection arithmetic is needed.

12198               	; 	' and Harry white, but this is the TMS9918's two-colours-per-8x1-cell
12199               	; 	' mode: a black dot and a white dot on the same pixel row of the same
12200               	; 	' character cannot both exist. Blinking distinguishes them with one
12201               	; 	' colour, which is what RallyX does with its player dot.

12205               	; 	' the lot: 96 bytes, no name-table traffic, and the same cost whether one
12206               	; 	' flight is visible or ten. The phases slide the cells ALONG the slope, so

12234               	; 	' 8 px period, so advancing by the frame delta ALIASES: at fdv 2 the
12235               	; 	' pattern flips between two positions half a period apart and the
12236               	; 	' direction stops being readable, and at fdv 3 the sequence runs 0,3,2,1
12237               	; 	' -- the staircase visibly runs BACKWARDS, carrying its steps down while
12238               	; 	' the rider goes up. That is the wagon-wheel effect, and no amount of
12239               	; 	' phase arithmetic fixes it: a 4-phase cycle can only be stepped by 1.
12240               	; 	'
12241               	; 	' So the ANIMATION is the clock here, and the rider is paced from it --
12242               	; 	' see move_kelly, which advances him by the same fixed 2-and-1 per pass
12243               	; 	' rather than by fdv. Locking the two together is the only way they
12244               	; 	' cannot drift, and it is what "the player moves at the rate the steps
12245               	; 	' carry him" actually means. The cost is that a ride takes 36 passes
12246               	; 	' rather than 36 frames, so it slows down when the loop does -- which is

12544               	;
12545               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------- the scanner's furniture
12546               	; 	' Without this the scanner is two dots in a void: you can see THAT Harry is
12547               	; 	' somewhere, but not what he is near, which is the one thing you actually
12548               	; 	' need when he is off-screen. Floor lines say which level, the slashes say
12549               	; 	' where that floor's escalator is, and the bar says where the elevator is --
12550               	; 	' exactly the three things the manual lists.
12551               	; 	'
12552               	; 	' FURNITURE AND DOTS ARE SEGREGATED BY PIXEL ROW ON PURPOSE, and a level
12553               	; 	' band is now FOUR rows, one per colour, because a pixel row carries
12554               	; 	' exactly one colour here:
12555               	; 	'
12556               	; 	'   +0  GREY    escalator head, and the elevator car
12557               	; 	'   +1  GREY    the air of that floor
12558               	; 	'   +2  GREY
12559               	; 	'   +3  YELLOW  the floor line -- and NOTHING else goes here
12560               	; 	'
12561               	; 	' THE FIRST THREE ROWS ARE THE FLOOR'S AIR AND EVERYTHING LIVES IN THEM:
12562               	; 	' the escalator's three-step diagonal, the lift car, and both actors, all
12563               	; 	' three pixels tall. They are grey in the table, and the Kop and the
12564               	; 	' crook recolour their own CHARACTER as they move (scan_mark) -- which is
12565               	; 	' what lets both of them fill the band instead of getting a pixel row
12566               	; 	' each. Eight pixels of this canvas is half a screen of the store, so
12567               	; 	' they are almost never in one character; when they are, they merge.
12568               	; 	'
12569               	; 	' Shrinking from six rows bought eight empty pixel rows, four above the
12570               	; 	' instrument and four below, so it no longer butts against the shop floor
12571               	; 	' above it or the bottom of the screen.
12572               	; 	'
12573               	; 	' The dots are erased by ANDing their bits out, so anything sharing a row
12574               	; 	' with one is rubbed away wherever an actor has passed -- which is why
12575               	; 	' scan_escs and scan_elev redraw every tick rather than once.

12917               	;
12918               	; 	' Blank the canvas by WRITING zeros rather than copying 384 of them out
12919               	; 	' of ROM. This runs twice a game -- at setup and on a new Krook -- so a
12920               	; 	' loop costs nothing anybody can perceive, and it hands the fixed area
12921               	; 	' back the best part of half a kilobyte, which is the budget that
12922               	; 	' actually binds. Paced in bursts: a few hundred VDP writes in a single
12923               	; 	' frame are silently dropped (CLAUDE.md 3A).
12924               	; scan_wipe:
12925               cvb_SCAN_WIPE
12926               	; 	' THIS ADDRESS IS A CHARACTER CODE IN DISGUISE, AND IT WENT STALE.
12927               	; 	' 4096 is the pattern table's BOTTOM THIRD -- rows 16-23, which is
12928               	; 	' band 0 and the radar together -- and the canvas characters begin at
12929               	; 	' genart's SCAN_FIRST, so the base is 4096 + SCAN_FIRST*8. It was
12930               	; 	' written out by hand as 4096 + 160*8 when SCAN_FIRST was 160; art
12931               	; 	' added later moved SCAN_FIRST to 208 and nothing moved this with it,
12932               	; 	' so the wipe zeroed the 48 characters BELOW the canvas and never
12933               	; 	' touched the canvas at all.
12934               	; 	'
12935               	; 	' Two of those forty-eight are STRUCTURE. ENDWALL is the building's
12936               	; 	' outside wall and SLABP is a pillar's cap. Blanking a pattern in ONE
12937               	; 	' THIRD leaves a character that draws correctly everywhere else and
12938               	; 	' falls back to its own background colour here -- so the GROUND FLOOR's
12939               	; 	' outside wall turned into plain green while the identical wall one
12940               	; 	' storey up was perfect, and the ground floor's pillars lost the brick
12941               	; 	' carried up through the bar above them. ENDWALL appears only on
12942               	; 	' screens 0 and 7, which is exactly why it was reported as happening
12943               	; 	' only on the escalator screens, mirrored side to side.
12944               	; 	'
12945               	; 	' The name table was correct the whole time. Probing it said so, four
12946               	; 	' times. It was the GLYPH that was empty, in one third only -- which a
12947               	; 	' probe that copies the character somewhere else to look at it cannot
12948               	; 	' see, because the copy renders from a different third's pattern.
12949               	; 	'
12950               	; 	' renumber.py rewrites this line from genart.SCAN_FIRST, and
12951               	; 	' checkstruct.py fails the build if the two disagree.

13024               	; 	' flights and the lift car do not move relative to the canvas, so they
13025               	; 	' are pixels in the scanner's own characters and cost nothing to keep.
13026               	; 	' The Kop and the crook DO move, and as sprites they need no colour
13027               	; 	' table, no erase and no priority arithmetic -- they draw over the
13028               	; 	' furniture because sprites always do, and nothing shifts to make room.
13029               	; 	'

13031               	; 	' canvas can only carry one colour, so at close range the two markers
13032               	; 	' merged and the blink was the only thing left to tell them apart. Two
13033               	; 	' sprites are two colours wherever they stand.

13035               	; 	' The furniture is drawn ONCE, by scan_furn. It used to be redrawn every
13036               	; 	' tick because erasing a character-based marker ANDed bits out of
13037               	; 	' whatever it was standing on; there is nothing left to rub it away. The
13038               	; 	' car still redraws itself, because the car actually moves.
13039               	; 	' -- the lift car. IT WAS FLICKERING, and the cause was not the drawing
13040               	; 	' but the ERASING: scan_elev cleared its three cells and put them back
13041               	; 	' every tick, whether or not the car had moved, so several times a second

13829               	;
13830               	; 	' THE BONUS IS COUNTED OUT, NOT AWARDED. Dropping the whole sum into the
13831               	; 	' score in one frame tells the player a number; ticking the clock down a
13832               	; 	' unit at a time, with the score climbing and a beat under each step,
13833               	; 	' tells them what the number was FOR. It is the pay-off for every second
13834               	; 	' they saved, and every arcade game of this era spends a moment on it.
13835               	; 	'
13836               	; 	' It also costs nothing to get right: the loop already has to run down
13837               	; 	' `tsec`, so the animation IS the calculation, and the repeated-addition
13838               	; 	' note below stops applying -- each step adds one band's worth.
13839               	; 	'
13840               	; 	' x100 for Krooks 1-9, x200 for 10-15, x300 from 16. Two independent
13841               	; 	' sources agree on those bands; the manual's own wording suggests
13842               	; 	' 1-8 / 9-16 / 17+ and DESIGN.md 0 records the disagreement.
13843               	; 	'
13844               	; 	' IN UNITS OF TEN, WHICH IS WHAT THE SCORE IS COUNTED IN, so the bands are
13845               	; 	' 10 / 20 / 30 and not 100 / 200 / 300.
13846               	; 	'
13847               	; 	' They were 100 / 200 / 300 and paid TEN TIMES the right bonus -- 1,000 a
13848               	; 	' time unit where the original pays 100. `add_score` takes `#addv` in units
13849               	; 	' of ten (the prize beside it is `#addv = 5` for fifty points, and the bonus
13850               	; 	' Kop threshold is `#nextk = 1000` for ten thousand), so writing the band in
13851               	; 	' POINTS here shifted every tally one decimal place. Reported from play as
13852               	; 	' "it seems like you awarded 1000 per time unit left" -- exactly right.
13853               	; 	'
13854               	; 	' Nothing failed: 1,000 a unit is a plausible-looking number, the digits
13855               	; 	' all line up, and the only symptom is a score that runs away. The tell is
13856               	; 	' a constant written in a different unit from the routine it is passed to,
13857               	; 	' which is the same class of fault as the px-per-pass speeds in 3A.
13858               	; 	'
13859               	; 	' (This is also why the old comment here said "#bval MUST BE 16-BIT: 300
13860               	; 	' does not fit in a byte". At 10 / 20 / 30 it would, but it stays 16-bit
13861               	; 	' because `#addv` is, and a byte here would buy two bytes of ROM in
13862               	; 	' exchange for a truncation trap the next time somebody edits a band.)

13979               	;
13980               	; 	' AND IT ENDS ON ITS LAST BLIP -- there is no closing accent.
13981               	; 	'
13982               	; 	' Two were tried. The bench's own ending for this variant rose a fourth,
13983               	; 	' to 2,542 Hz, and a square wave there is a shriek -- the same fault the
13984               	; 	' pickup was rewritten for. Dropping it an OCTAVE BELOW the ticks, to
13985               	; 	' 518 Hz, was reported the same way, and that one cannot be too high by
13986               	; 	' any measure: it is the lowest note in the effect.
13987               	; 	'
13988               	; 	' So the complaint is not the pitch, it is the extra note. A tally is
13989               	; 	' arithmetic, and arithmetic finishes when the last term is added; a
13990               	; 	' flourish after it is a second event the player has to interpret, and
13991               	; 	' the HUD has already said the clock is empty. The count stops when the
13992               	; 	' counting stops.
13993               	;
13994               	; 	' `calc_bonus` USED TO LIVE HERE and computed the whole sum by repeated
13995               	; 	' addition, to dodge two hazards at once: `tsec * bmul` is an 8-bit
13996               	; 	' product (a 50-unit capture in the x300 band pays 15,000, six times past
13997               	; 	' a byte), and multiplying properly lands on the MPY/r0 hazard where a
13998               	; 	' 16-bit variable read straight after being multiplied returns the
13999               	; 	' product's high word. Counting the bonus out a unit at a time (above)
14000               	; 	' removes the multiply entirely rather than working around it -- the loop
14001               	; 	' the player watches IS the arithmetic.
14002               	; 	'
14003               	; 	' It also fixed the last-tick case for free: `bn_loop` tests `tsec = 0`
14004               	; 	' on entry, where the old `FOR bi = 1 TO tsec` would have run its body
14005               	; 	' once and paid a full multiplier for no time at all (CLAUDE.md 3A).

14050               	; 	' THE CAST IS NOT TAKEN AWAY YET -- hide_all now runs AFTER the beat.
14051               	; 	'
14052               	; 	' It used to run here, so the moment the clock emptied, Harry and the
14053               	; 	' thing that had just hit him vanished and the sound played over an empty
14054               	; 	' store. The hit that ENDS a round is the worst case: `do_hit` sets tout
14055               	; 	' before the freeze starts and the main loop leaves on the very next pass,
14056               	; 	' so the hit sound gets one tick and everything is already gone.
14057               	; 	'
14058               	; 	' The pause drains the sound; leaving the actors up means it drains over
14059               	; 	' the picture that caused it. Nothing is moving -- the pause ticks sfx_tick
14060               	; 	' and nothing else -- so it is a held tableau, not a frozen game.
14061               	; 	' THE MESSAGE BOX, ON THE GAME SCREEN AND NOT INSTEAD OF IT.
14062               	; 	'
14063               	; 	' It used to CLS before GAME OVER, so the last thing the player saw was
14064               	; 	' the store being deleted and then two words on an empty field -- which
14065               	; 	' reads as the program ending rather than as the game ending. The store
14066               	; 	' stays; the message sits in the middle of it.
14067               	; 	'
14068               	; 	' THE BOX IS THE FONT'S OWN BACKGROUND. Every font character is black on
14069               	; 	' HUD_BG (dark blue), so a row of SPACES is a solid dark blue bar. A blank
14070               	; 	' row above and below the text is a frame for the price of two strings and
14071               	; 	' no new characters, and it reads against the store because nothing else on
14072               	; 	' the playfield is that colour.
14073               	; 	'
14074               	; 	' THIRTEEN WIDE, WHICH IS THE LONGEST MESSAGE PLUS ONE EITHER SIDE.
14075               	; 	' HE GOT AWAY and THE BIPLANE are both eleven. Every string below is padded
14076               	; 	' to exactly thirteen so the box has straight edges, and column 10 puts it
14077               	; 	' at columns 10-22 -- centre 16, the screen's.
14078               	; 	'
14079               	; 	' THE REASON IS ALWAYS ON THE SAME ROW, and that is what lets one layout
14080               	; 	' serve both cases. Losing a life draws three rows around it; losing the
14081               	; 	' last one draws two more ON TOP, so GAME OVER appears above the reason
14082               	; 	' rather than replacing it. Printing the reason at a different row for each
14083               	; 	' case would need `PRINT AT` with a variable, and every other PRINT in this
14084               	; 	' program uses a constant.

14305               	;
14306               	; 	' A SOUND STILL PLAYING WHEN THE ROUND ENDS IS ALLOWED TO FINISH.
14307               	; 	'
14308               	; 	' This used to open with a bare `GOSUB snd_off`, which cut it dead. That
14309               	; 	' was not an accident: the decay counters are ticked by the MAIN LOOP, and
14310               	; 	' this pause REPLACES the main loop, so a tone left latched with nothing
14311               	; 	' ticking it hangs for the full ninety frames -- the sticky-audio failure
14312               	; 	' this game has already shipped twice. The answer is to DRAIN the counters
14313               	; 	' rather than to stop silencing.
14314               	; 	'
14315               	; 	' CLEAR THE PENDING LATCHES FIRST. sf* flags are sounds that have not
14316               	; 	' happened yet; left set, the drain below would START one and the pause
14317               	; 	' would end with a fresh note ringing into the next round.
14318               	; 	'
14319               	; 	' THEN TICK sfx_tick WHOLE, not some decay-only part of it. The five
14320               	; 	' counters do not all live in one place: sot, sht and spt are a block at
14321               	; 	' the tail, but spz (the prize arpeggio) and swt (the jump warble) tick up
14322               	; 	' among the code that starts sounds. Draining only the tail would finish a
14323               	; 	' footstep and still cut the arpeggio, which is the one effect with a
14324               	; 	' phrase worth saving. Calling the whole routine also leaves the write
14325               	; 	' order on CHANNEL 2 alone, which spz and spt share.
14326               	; 	'
14327               	; 	' EVERY THIRD FRAME, because the main loop runs about 2.5 frames per pass
14328               	; 	' and this loop waits one frame per turn. Ticking every frame would play
14329               	; 	' everything at two and a half times its tuned speed. Three frames a tick
14330               	; 	' is ~17% slow and gives 30 ticks against the longest effect's 20 passes.
14331               	; 	'
14332               	; 	' THE LOOP COUNTS TICKS, NOT FRAMES, which is what makes the pacing free.
14333               	; 	' Counting 91 frames and firing on every third needs a second counter, an
14334               	; 	' increment and a test -- 48 bytes, on a fixed area with 66 left. Counting
14335               	; 	' 31 TICKS of three WAITs each is the same 93 frames and the same three
14336               	; 	' frames per tick, with none of that. The duration changes by two frames.
14337               	; 	'
14338               	; 	' snd_off still runs at the END, as the backstop for anything the drain
14339               	; 	' did not finish.
14340               	; pause_beat:
14341               cvb_PAUSE_BEAT

14703               	;
14704               	; 	' THE LOW-TIME WARNING IS SILENT. There was a beep a second under ten, and
14705               	; 	' it was the wrong instrument for the job: the last ten seconds are the
14706               	; 	' busiest part of a round, so a repeating tone arrives exactly when the
14707               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
14708               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
14709               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
14710               	;
14711               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
14712               	; 	'
14713               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
14714               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
14715               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
14716               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
14717               	; 	'
14718               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
14719               	; 	'
14720               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
14721               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
14722               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
14723               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
14724               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
14725               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
14726               	; 	'
14727               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
14728               	; 	'
14729               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
14730               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
14731               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
14732               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
14733               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
14734               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
14735               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
14736               	; 	'
14737               	; 	' MEASURED OFF THE COLECOVISION: 14 px, about 7.4 a second.
14738               	; 	'
14739               	; 	' It was 15 px and 6.9 a second, picked between an 8.0 that read as
14740               	; 	' slightly hurried and a 6.1 that read as trudging -- a judgement between
14741               	; 	' two other judgements, with nothing underneath it. The ColecoVision
14742               	; 	' recording settles it: footfalls land every 0.130 s across a twelve-second
14743               	; 	' continuous run, which is 7.7 a second, and that is the one finding in the
14744               	; 	' whole sound analysis the method resolves EXACTLY -- a rhythm rather than a
14745               	; 	' pitch, counted off the RMS track rather than inferred from a spectrum.
14746               	; 	' (colecosounds variant 1A; assets/sfx/sfxref-coleco.md has the working.)
14747               	; 	'
14748               	; 	' 104 px/s over 14 px is 7.43 a second. 13 px would give 8.00, and 7.7 sits
14749               	; 	' almost exactly between them -- so this is the nearer of the two, and it is
14750               	; 	' also the one that does not walk back into the 8.0 that was rejected by ear.
14751               	; 	'
14752               	; 	' WHY THE GAME KEEPS A DISTANCE AND THE BENCH KEEPS A CADENCE. The bench
14753               	; 	' plays a fixed eight frames between steps because it has no walking to tie
14754               	; 	' them to; the game accumulates PIXELS TRAVELLED, so the feet keep time with
14755               	; 	' the legs when he is slowed or stopped. Matching "7.4 a second" therefore
14756               	; 	' means matching it AT HIS WALKING SPEED, and assumes the ColecoVision's
14757               	; 	' crook walks at ours -- which the recording cannot confirm.
14758               	; 	'
14759               	; 	' The dial is this one constant and the subtraction below, which must stay
14760               	; 	' threshold + 1 or the carry is wrong.
14761               	; 	'
14762               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
14763               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to
14764               	; 	' zero on the pass that set it and the note-off fires before the sound has
14765               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of
14766               	; 	' sound -- about 42 ms against the bench's 33, as close as a per-pass timer
14767               	; 	' gets, and the reason the bench and the game cannot sound identical.
14768               	; 	'
14769               	; 	' Register 4 is white noise at the fastest rate.
14770               	; 	'
14771               	; 	' VOLUME 9, WHICH IS UNDER EVERYTHING ELSE ON PURPOSE. The hit, the prize
14772               	; 	' and the jump are 12 and 13, and they happen ONCE; footsteps play for the
14773               	; 	' whole round. At 13 they were level with the events they are supposed to
14774               	; 	' sit beneath, so the effects that carry information had nothing to stand

14976               	;
14977               	; 	' EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS ASSEMBLED INTO BANK 1, so the INCLUDE order
14978               	; 	' is load-bearing and nothing but data may follow it.
14979               	; 	'
14980               	; 	' THE FONT IS NOW IN THE BANK TOO, and it used to be deliberately outside:
14981               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
14982               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
14983               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
14984               	; 	'
14985               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
14986               	; 	'
14987               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
14988               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
14989               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
14990               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
14991               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
14992               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
14993               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
14994               	; 	'
14995               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
14996               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
14997               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
14998               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
14999               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
15000               	; 	'
15001               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
15002               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
15003               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
15004               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
15005               	; 	#if TI994A
15006               	; 	BANK 2
15007      0110     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$

15145               	;
15146               	; 	' THE COLOUR TABLE, 472 bytes of the same value ($14 = black ink on dark blue).
15147               	; 	'
15148               	; 	' Loaded with DEFINE COLOR 32,59,font_col, which is ONE synchronous call that
15149               	; 	' writes all three screen thirds (define_color always does the LDIRVM3 triple
15150               	; 	' copy). It replaced a VPOKE loop that wrote this one value 1,416 times paced by
15151               	; 	' 24 WAITs -- the largest scripted delay in the boot, and the reason the title
15152               	; 	' screen used to fill in visibly rather than appearing at once.
15153               	; 	'
15154               	; 	' EIGHT BYTES PER CHARACTER, not one. Supply fewer and DEFINE COLOR reads
15155               	; 	' whatever follows in ROM as colour data, with no error at build or run time.
15156               	;
15157               	; font_col:
15158               cvb_FONT_COL

15671               	; 	INCLUDE "art.bas"
15672               	; 	' Keystone Kapers art -- GENERATED by assets/genart.py. Do not edit; regenerate.
15673               	; 	'
15674               	; 	' EVERY SPRITE IS 16x16: sprite size and magnification are GLOBAL on the
15675               	; 	' TMS9918, so small objects are drawn small INSIDE a 16x16 box rather than
15676               	; 	' being small sprites.
15677               	; 	'
15678               	; 	' EVERY 8-PX OBJECT SITS IN ROWS 8-15 OF ITS BOX, ducked Kelly included, so
15679               	; 	' one rule places them all: bottom edge = y + 16, and a thing resting on the
15680               	; 	' floor is at y = FLOORY - 16.
15681               	; 	'
15682               	; 	' Sprite bytes are QUADRANT-ORDERED: 16 rows of the left half, then 16 of
15683               	; 	' the right. Every block is an EVEN number of bytes -- an odd DATA BYTE run
15684               	; 	' silently misaligns every word table after it (CLAUDE.md 3A).
15685               	;
15686               	; spr_kelly:	' Kelly: RIGHT hat/face/tunic/tunic-arm-up/duck-hat/duck-face, then the same LEFT (+24), then the FOUR shared run frames. Patterns 0..60
15687               cvb_SPR_KELLY

16943               	; 	INCLUDE "store.bas"
16944               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
16945               	; 	'
16946               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
16947               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
16948               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
16949               	; 	'
16950               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
16951               	; 	' blit is
16952               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
16953               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
16954               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
16955               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
16956               	; 	'
16957               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
16958               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
16959               	; 	'
16960               	; 	' template ids:
16961               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
16962               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B
16963               	; 	'   2 T_ESC_W
16964               	; 	'   3 T_ESC_E
16965               	; 	'   4 T_ELEV
16966               	; 	'   5 T_ROOF0
16967               	; 	'   6 T_ROOF1
16968               	; 	'   7 T_ROOF2
16969               	; 	'   8 T_ROOF3
16970               	; 	'   9 T_ROOF4
16971               	; 	'   10 T_ROOF5
16972               	; 	'   11 T_ROOF6
16973               	; 	'   12 T_ROOF7
16974               	; 	'   13 T_END_W
16975               	; 	'   14 T_END_E
16976               	;
16977               	; stor_tpl:	' 15 templates x 160 bytes
